title: KMS Evidence Serialization and RBACv2 Claims Spec
body:
Purpose:
This spec standardizes how Redwood serializes cryptographic evidence derived from KMS/HSM operations for downstream RBACv2 attestation, SIEM ingestion, and long-term archival. It focuses on: (1) canonical event shape for audit events, (2) RBACv2 claim mappings needed for key custody checks, (3) evidence collection automation recipes, and (4) HSM fallback/verification sequences for rotation windows and BYOK onboarding.

Scope:
Applies to: hosted API key material, dedicated and private deployments using Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs/BYOK), HSM-bound master keys, and transient/ephemeral keys used by serving runtime. Excludes application-level data encryption patterns that do not touch KMS/HSM.

Background and goals:
- Provide a minimal, verifiable JSON shape that SIEM and Evidence Store can index efficiently.
- Ensure RBACv2 claims are emitted with each evidence bundle so policy engines can validate whether a key action was authorized.
- Enable automated testable checks after rotation or failover (integrated into CI and ops runbooks).

Key concepts and identifiers:
- key_id: stable UUID v4, not human-friendly. Format: key://{region}/{tenant_id}/{key_uuid} e.g. key://us-west-2/t-1234/7f3b9e2a-...
- key_version: semantic string, e.g. v1, v1-2024-11-21
- material_origin: one of [redwood-kms, customer-byok, hsm-ns0]
- custodian_principal: RBACv2 principal id (format: user|service|role:{id})

RBACv2 claims mapping (fields emitted with evidence):
- rbac_claims.principal_id -> custodian_principal (string)
- rbac_claims.action -> enum [key:generate, key:rotate, key:revoke, key:export, key:assign-policy]
- rbac_claims.policy_version -> policy hash or id (string)
- rbac_claims.mfa -> boolean or method string (e.g., 'webauthn')
- rbac_claims.scope -> list of strings (e.g., [tenant, project, environment])
Note: Emit full principal chain for cross-team operations: principal_chain -> ["role:sec-admin:alice","service:rotation-agent"]

Canonical audit event JSON (stringified in SIEM body):
{
  "event_type": "kms.key.operation",
  "timestamp": "2024-11-21T14:32:10Z",
  "key_id": "key://us-west-2/t-1234/7f3b9e2a-...",
  "key_version": "v1-2024-11-21",
  "operation": "key:rotate",
  "status": "success",
  "material_origin": "hsm-ns0",
  "initiator": "service:rotation-agent",
  "rbac_claims": {
    "principal_id": "role:sec-admin:alice",
    "action": "key:rotate",
    "policy_version": "policy-9c4f",
    "mfa": "webauthn",
    "scope": ["t-1234","project-inference"]
  },
  "evidence_links": ["s3://evidence-prod/keys/t-1234/7f3b9e.../bundle-20241121.tar.gz"],
  "hashes": {"manifest_sha256": "...", "key_thumbprint": "..."},
  "notes": "rotation triggered by scheduled policy; automatic canary verify queued"
}

SIEM ingestion mapping guide:
- Index fields: event_type, timestamp, key_id (tokenize on /), operation, status, initiator, material_origin, rbac_claims.principal_id, rbac_claims.action, manifest_sha256.
- Alert rules: (1) key:export by non-admin principal -> immediate P1; (2) rotate failure > 3 attempts -> P1; (3) BYOK upload with missing HSM-attestation -> P2.
- Recommended ingestion: bulk compress bundles for evidence storage, push event metadata to SIEM (no raw key material). Evidence store should be treated as separate S3 bucket with restricted access and WORM-like retention.

Evidence bundle composition (archive stored off-SIEM):
- manifest.json (includes list of files, offsets, hashes, key_id, key_version, material_origin)
- acsk_attestation.txt (HSM attestation statements, where applicable)
- rotation_trace.log (detailed command/response trace with timestamps)
- rbacsnap.json (snapshot of RBACv2 claim resolution at moment of operation)
- canary_verification.json (results of sample decryption/signature test)

Automation recipes (ops runbook snippets):
1) Rotation automation should produce: manifest.json, rbacsnap.json, hashes, then atomically upload bundle to evidence S3 and emit SIEM event with evidence_links.
2) Verification pipeline: after rotation, run canary using temporary ephemeral key_version; record canary results to canary_verification.json and push metric to datadog: kms.rotation.canary.{success|failure}.
3) Evidence retention policy: default 2 years for tenant keys; HIPAA/PDF regulated tenants up to 7 years (config per tenant metadata).

HSM fallback choreography for failed rotations:
- Detect failure (rotation agent sees non-idempotent state) -> mark key as 'rotation-in-progress' and notify SRE + custodian via PagerDuty.
- Snapshot RBAC resolution and export rbacsnap.json immediately.
- If HSM node unresponsive, attempt fallback to secondary HSM pool with approved cross-signing; if fallback fails, enter 'degraded' state and publish SIEM event event_type: kms.key.failover.requested with reason.
- Post-incident forensics: run the evidence collector with flags --include-volatility --collect-processes and attach results to incident ticket.

BYOK onboarding checklist (brief):
- Tenant provides key material in wrapped form and KMS metadata.
- Validate attestation: if HSM-backed, require vendor attestation blob and parse into acsk_attestation.txt.
- Run rbacsnap resolution: ensure at least one custodian_principal has role:byok-approver.
- Emit SIEM event key:byok.upload with masked key identifier and evidence_links.

Verification and offline attestations:
- All manifests must include a manifest_sha256. Evidence store computes archive-level sha256 and publishes difference if any.
- For critical rotations, require dual-operator approval: both principals' rbacsnap chains must be present and signed.

Operational queries and dashboards (plausible list):
- Rotation success rate by region/tenant (90d window)
- Average time between rotation start and canary success
- Number of key:export events by principal (alert when > 0 for non-admins)
- Evidence ingestion lag (time between operation timestamp and evidence bundle available)

Developer notes and integration points:
- SDK: evidence bundle uploader lives in github.com/redwood-inference/kms-evidence-automation. Use client.upload_bundle(manifest, files) which returns evidence_links array to include in emitted event.
- RBACv2: ensure policy engine can produce policy_version hashes; include GUID mapping for legacy policies.
- SIEM: ingest must validate manifest_sha256 and reject events pointing to missing evidence.

Open questions and TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Should we include partial encrypted material for faster offline verification? (privacy vs. verification tradeoff)
- Standardize tenant-specific retention overrides in tenant metadata API (currently ad-hoc).
- Define archival format for multi-year WORM compliance across regions.

Appendix: sample rbacsnap.json (abbreviated):
{
  "resolved_at": "2024-11-21T14:31:50Z",
  "key_id": "key://us-west-2/t-1234/7f3b9e2a-...",
  "principal_chain": ["role:sec-admin:alice","service:rotation-agent"],
  "policies": [{"id":"policy-9c4f","hash":"9c4f...","perms":["rotate","assign-policy"]}]
}

This document is purposely prescriptive about emitted claims and evidence composition to make downstream verification deterministic. Feedback requested from platform-engineering (integration tests for uploader), SRE (failover scenarios), and compliance (retention and WORM requirements).
